claims.claim: Offline cracking cost per guess ~ KDF cost
claims.evidence_quote: It makes calculating the hash more computationally expensive, which in turn reduces the speed and/or increases the cost for which an attacker can attempt to crack the password hash.
claims.note: From OWASP's Using Work Factors section: 'The work factor is the number of iterations of the hashing algorithm that are performed for each password', and higher work factors 'make hashes more difficult for an attacker to crack'.

coverage: I took the frontmatter description and every sentence of the incident narrative, exposure equation, response playbook and prevention bullets - the 2022 dating, the vault-backup theft, unencrypted URLs, the 1 and 5,000 iteration counts, the unmigrated-defaults history, the researcher-linked crypto thefts, the diceware 6-word/77-bit and 8-character figures, the ~12-character and ~100,000-iteration thresholds, the rotation order, TOTP re-enrolment, the provider/KDF move, session revocation, the offline-cracking line and both prevention bullets - so that every number, threshold and behaviour is covered, and checked each against all three listed sources fetched today; blog.lastpass.com was readable via the web fetch tool and plain urllib but returns 403 to attest.py's wavefront-attest/1 user agent (retested twice, and 403 also for a browser-like UA), so it is omitted from sources and its claims are gated rather than confirmed; the Verify checklist items are to-dos, not factual claims, and were excluded.
suggested_edits: Nothing is contradicted, but only 1 of 20 claims is confirmed from a re-fetchable source and 3 are gated: blog.lastpass.com blocks attest.py's wavefront-attest/1 fetcher with 403 (also 403 for a browser-like UA, though readable via the web fetch tool and plain urllib), so the incident-notice claims - vault backups copied in 2022, unencrypted URLs alongside encrypted passwords and notes, and the ~12-character and ~100,000-iteration thresholds traceable to the notice's twelve-character minimum and 100,100-iteration default - are gated rather than confirmed, and re-fetch checks of that source will fail in this environment. Uncovered by any listed source: the 1-or-5,000 iteration figures and unmigrated-defaults history, the researcher-linked crypto thefts, the diceware 77-bit and 8-character figures, the whole response playbook (rotation order, TOTP re-enrolment, provider/KDF move with a new master password, session revocation and email-forwarding review) and both prevention bullets. A fix PR should bump version and either add sources covering them - LastPass's later March 2023 update or third-party reporting for the iteration history and crypto-theft link, an EFF diceware reference for the entropy figure, a breach-response guide for the playbook - or trim those sections to what the current sources support.
